column3: Hello, I'm Arthur Ackerman.
YOU'LL HAVE TO SPEAK UP, DEAR!
I'm a little hard of hearing, you see.
Sorry, I'm Arthur Ackerman!
WHO'S THAT?
It's me! I'm an attorney at law!
YOU'RE A TERRIBLE BORE?
Are you doing this on purpose?
Hehe, who's to say?
Now, what is it you want?
Hello again.
What is it you want, Arthur?
Hey! You're looking a little worse for wear there, pal.
I'm ferfectly pine, I asshure you.
Here's a coffee, on the house.
Thanksh!
Evening, Barkeep!
What'll it be?
That's the plant fibres, and the floral essence, accounted for.
Everything I need to make a Rosebud.
Now, I can't legally give you the real deal if you're anywhere under 200lbs.
Your liver would give in.
So what can you give me?
I'll make you a Bud-Lite.
It has all of the flavour of the Rosebud.
But you'll still be able to...
Form sentences?
Precisely.
It's delicious!
Enjoy!
I might be able to make it stronger with some experimentation.
And something to mix it all up in.
Waasch schup?
Sorry old chap!
Can't understand a word!
Hello!
Ah, Ackerman, isn't it?
Arthur A. Ackerman, at your service.
I'm Kasper Bergmann, the treasurer of the Lady Unterwald estate.
Can you believe it, Arthur? What a messy state of affairs we've found ourselves in.
My feelings exactly.
Is there something I can help you with?
Hello again, Arthur.
How can I help you?
What do you make of this ledger, Bergmann?
Wh- Where did you get that!
I found it sealed away in the bottom of a locked drawer.
H- How peculiar! I've never seen that before in my life!
Really? Then we should pass this to the authorities when they arrive.
No!
I'd bet if they were to audit this ledger, the numbers wouldn't add up.
Listen, Arthur. I'm in a bit of a bind here.
Ashamed to say, I've fallen in with a rather unscrupulous individual.
Are you talking about Donny Donato?
I'm afraid so.
They managed to exploit my weakness, don't you see?
I'm a victim in all this, Arthur!
It's time to come clean. What's going on?
It's Donny. He's concocted a scheme to cheat at the casino tables.
We need to stop him, Arthur. I can't afford to lose more of the estate's money.
Ah, the man behind the curtain!
As I live and breathe.
I was starting to think you were just a disembodied limb with anger issues!
Yeah, well I'm sorry to disappoint you.
Just tell me, how'd you figure out the five-fingered handshake of formality?
Good evening, kid.
Having a good time, sir?
Oh dear, now there's another one!
Go and sober up on the sofa, Mr Ackerman.
Hey there.
Greetings.
I'm Brother Jared, Custodian of the Silken Palms.
How can I be of assistance?
Good evening, hun.
Do you have any winnings?
Oh, no I'm not the gambling type.
Well, bring any chips to me and I'll convert them into cash for you!
As a matter of fact, I do.
Great! How much do you want to exchange?
Congratulations again on your big win.
Thanks!
Are you ignoring me?
Hey.
Buzz off, kid.
I won't ask nicely again.
I'd better not anger him further.
What did you do with Donny Donato?
The casino cheat? He's been handled.
Handled? That sounds ominous.
What did you really do with Donny? Is he safe?
You ask too many questions.
Keep talking like that, maybe you'll find out first-hand.
I'd better not.
Hi there.
Do you not want to talk to me?
Hello again, friend.
Don't push your luck, pal.
Now I'm starting to get mad.
Probably best to leave him alone.
Where are you holding Donny Donato?
He won't be a problem for the casino going forward.
Is Donny still aboard the train, at least?
Were you a close associate of this casino cheat?
Are you going to be a problem that needs solving?
No, that won't be necessary!
I really shouldn't bother them again.
Oh, my beauty, what have they done to you?
Oui ?
Hello again, attorney.
Don't sneak up on me like that!
Ahh! You gave me a fright!
How can I help?
I can't understand you, sorry.
Did you find anything yet, Arthur?
We need to get that will back, Arthur.
Keep your guard up.
I'll monitor the situation from here.
We need to look into this further, Arthur.
Well, I've got Herman's keys.
Maybe we can look for evidence in his room?
The will is still missing.
Have you seen it anywhere, Arthur?
The missing will was here all along.
Better grab it before we lose it again, Arthur.
No, thanks!
What is this?
Not here.
I really don't want to touch that.
You hang on to it, Arthur.
The name's Donnola, kid.
But most people call me Don, or Donny. You get my gist?
That's a nice suit. So what's your deal, you some sort of tycoon or something?
Well, not really. You see, there's this old lady who told me to put it on, and I-
Let me stop you there, I don't think I wanna know more.
Besides, you're killing my vibe with that sweet patootie over there, you dig?
You delivered my proposal yet, kid?
Oh, not yet.
You gotta give it to the dame behind me, ya dig?
Ehh, I'll talk to him later.
Come back when you've handed over that note.
Beat it kid, can't you see I'm on a winning streak?
Hey, while you're here, you could do me a little favour.
You take this note and give it to that dame behind me, will ya?
What is it?
It's a proposal of sorts, requesting we both make tracks to my suite.
You get my drift?
I don't like the sound of that.
Why is it so damp?
I soaked it in perfume. You don't know squat about wooing a dame, do ya?
Gross.
I wouldn't want him to know that I borrowed it.
But, maybe I can use this to foil his scheme.
Well, I-
'Atta boy!
You just watch and learn now.
So, dollface. How about it?
I don't write love letters for every broad I see, you know. You should be grateful!
In that case, allow me to show you my gratitude.
See you around, Arthur.
Ahh, unrequited love.
Sorry, sir. The lounge and beyond are strictly off limits for now.
But there's a killer on the loose!
I'm the only one who had access to Lady Unterwald's will. I could be next!
No exceptions.
Sorry about Lady Unterwald.
What do you want, Arthur?
Hello there.
What's going on?
Ahh! Nothing!
Nobody has seen Herman since he vanished.
We're very concerned for his well-being!
Now, if you'll excuse us, we're going to check his room.
How's the breaking and entering going?
Not now, Arthur! We're trying to concentrate!
You're scaring me!
He's scaring me more!
Not thissh again.
I see.
*sigh* Yes, very good.
I'm feeling lucky.
You said that last time!
Trust me, I've got a system.
That's what they all say.
Who's the suit?
You better not be bad luck, mister.
How are you holding up, doc?
Doctor?
I think he's too distraught to talk right now.
I really thought Herman would be able to help us.
Forgive me, Lady Unterwald! I let you down.
I should have done something!
Pull yourself together!
There's nothing I could've done!
My god! Are you okay, Arthur?
How can I help, Arthur?
Mmm-wah?
Mr Masson?
Muahh, I see you're enjoying my shignature drink?
Good man!
Ah, so you've finally schobered up?
Muah, of coursshe I haven't!
Don't you see? We're the ssschame amount of drunk.
Ohhh. I guess that makes sschense?
What do you want, my dear boy?
Thanks for the help, Mr Masson.
MmEmAAw! *Hic*
t *Hic*
Oh right.
I should leave him to rest.
Good evening, sir.
Very good, sir.
I'm sorry for your loss.
Monsieur, I've lost everything!
You must have been very close.
No, it's not that...
She owed me so much money!
I was going to get paid after the speech.
Oh.
There, there.
Not now, Monsieur. Can't you see I'm with my latest muse?
Oh, Pierre, you do know how to flatter me.
The name's Ron.
I'm Arthur Ackerman!
Can I help you, Arthur?
Mm-hmm.
Salutations!
I'm Sister Gretchen, chief officer of the itinerary!
I can't understand you, Arthur.
Arthur Ackerman, at your service.
Susanne Goldschmidt.
Do you need anything?
I heard about Lady Unterwald.
Not at the moment!
Until next time.
Lady Unterwald was murdered! What should I do?
Sorry to hear that, pal. If you suspect foul play, you could talk to the other passengers? Search around for clues, maybe?
I need another hint, what should I do!
Have you tried talking to everybody aboard the train? Searching Lady Unterwald's quarters might yield some results.
Head to Lady Unterwald's quarters, you might find some clues there!
Talk to the sleazy gentleman in the dining carriage, then follow his instructions.
I need to get into Lady Unterwald's room!
Looks like you'll have to get past the guard first. Can you distract them somehow?
I need another hint, how can I get past the guard?
Maybe you could convince them to leave their post. Do they have a weakness for anything?
The guard suffers from a fragrance allergy. Can you find something that would trigger it?
There's a sleazy gentleman in the dining carriage who may have what you need.
Get the perfumed note off the sleazy gentleman in the dining carriage. It should be potent enough to deal with the guard.
I've lost the will, how can I get it back?
Have you spotted it? The will might be flapping about somewhere.
I need another hint about the will.
Explore all the carriages, you might be able to grab it!
If you explore the carriages, you should be able to find it in the window!
I tried to get the will back, but it flew away!
There's a chance it flew by the sleeper carriage. Those rooms are locked though!
You'll have to gain access to passengers' quarters before you can get to the will.
You'll need to access Herman's quarters, too bad he lost his keys!
I found some keys, what should I do next?
Could you return those keys to their rightful owner?
I need another hint about the keys.
Those look like room keys. Can you locate the room number?
Those are Don's keys. Maybe find the right room and drop them off?
Where can I find Bergmann's ledger?
It sounds like Bergmann hid the ledger in a safe space.
I need another hint about the ledger.
The ledger is hidden in Lady Unterwald's quarters. But where?
Did you try looking in Lady Unterwald's desk drawer?
Lady Unterwald's drawer is locked, what do I do?
Perhaps you can find something to wedge it open?
I need another hint about the desk drawer.
I'll bet you could fit something thin and metal in between the gap.
If you wedged a metal hanger in there, I bet it'd open!
I found the ledger, what should I do with it?
You could use that ledger to apply some pressure, no doubt.
If Bergmann's been cooking the books, he wouldn't be too pleased to see that.
I'd confront Bergmann with it, let's see what he has to say for himself then!
How do I stop Don's scheme?
Have you observed Don at the roulette table? How is he manipulating the result?
I need another hint to stop Don's scheme!
Don's rigged the game with a magnetic ball. Can you disrupt the magnetic field?
A well-placed magnet of your own would likely throw off Don's scheme!
How do I stop Don getting more casino chips?
He must be getting them from somewhere! Is there a way to find out?
I need another hint to stop Don getting chips!
It looks like Don heads for his quarters, maybe you can beat him to it?
When Don leaves the table, get to his room before he does!
That's enough hints for now.
Your payment, surely you had something agreed in writing?
Alas, our arrangement was but a delicate dance of words.
You only had a verbal agreement?
Oui, but Lady Unterwald is no longer here to keep her word.
Never again, Monsieur.
Did you see anything suspicious during the speech?
As you know, I capture every detail in the frame, just as I see it.
But the lights went out moments before we went through that tunnel.
When we emerged, all I could see was that look of terror, frozen on her face.
You didn't see anybody get close to Lady Unterwald?
If somebody approached Lady Unterwald with a weapon, I would have captured it.
I assure you, nobody moves faster than I can speed paint!
Who do you think would want to harm Lady Unterwald?
Isn't it obvious? A rival artist, surely consumed by jealousy.
They would stop at nothing to ruin my livelihood!
Someone's been threatening you?
Well, no. But it's a chilling thought!
Won't you have to find yourself a new muse?
First things first. Much like the greats before me, I shall channel my suffering into art.
Only then can I begin the arduous task of finding myself a new muse.
There is something I'd like you to help me with.
Ahh, what is it that you wish to capture? The human condition?
I'll need to be paid in advance, and no, I don't work for exposure.
I can't afford to make that mistake again.
This commission, what would you take as payment?
I'll need an upfront cash payment. No cheques, IOU's or other empty promises.
Take care of yourself.
I bid you adieu.
Sorry, can't tell you. It's a secret.
Funny guy, thinking you can keep secrets from a secret society.
That's hilarious stuff.
You have to admit, it's a little funny.
I just asked around, it seemed pretty easy to pick up!
I don't believe it for a second. You've been talking to that blabbering Doctor, haven't you?
I'm afraid I can't say.
Ugh! What part of ‘secret handshake' does that guy not get?
The secret part, I assume.
Just a little something I like to call intuition.
Mm-hmm. I doubt that very much.
I paid the world's fastest painter to capture your moves!
Pfft, come on. Nobody is that fast!
So, what does The Order of Idle Hands actually do?
The order was set up as a secret committee of sorts. We worked to ensure Lady Unterwald's business affairs were smoothly orchestrated behind the scenes.
And how's that going?
It hasn't been our finest hour.
What will you do about Lady Unterwald's murder?
It's probably best we don't meddle any further. Not until Lady Unterwald's last will and testament is in our hands.
I'm looking for the Doctor's medical briefcase.
Doctor Hirsch misplaced his bag, huh?
Any unattended luggage is usually thrown back into the storage room.
You'd need a key to get in there, though.
Do you have any ideas on opening a locked safe?
Hmm. Got any explosives to hand?
No, I didn't think to bring any with me.
Too bad. In that case, you're playing by the safe's rules.
So you want to know how I figured out the handshake?
Go on.
I should be going.
Come and find us as soon as you've recovered that will, Arthur.
Custodian of the Silken Palms?
Oh yes!
Did you know the hands are the most used part of the body?
Is that true?
I'm the first line of defence against wrinkles, cracking and dehydration.
It's a lot of responsibility!
What does the Custodian of the Silken Palms do, exactly?
Cuticle care, nail filing, the odd hand massage here and there.
I've even formulated my own hand cream, packed with essential oils. It's known to boost moisture levels and skin elasticity!
They're quite therapeutic, you know!
Moisturised any hands lately?
Why, were you looking to make an appointment?
I'm sure I could squeeze you in!
Ah, that won't be necessary.
Another time, then!
What's that book you're reading?
Oh, this? It's Dr Phogg's Guide to Invis-Ability!
The title is written in invisible ink, see?
Hm, I don't see!
Exactly. That's how you know it's the real deal!
The Order has its handshakes, but secret messages? Invisible ink?
This is going to elevate us to a whole new level!
What's the book you're reading called again?
I still don't see it.
Exactly. It's Dr Phogg's Guide to Invis-Ability!
Does your guide book explain how to reveal hidden messages?
Well sure, there's a whole chapter on it!
But no spoilers, okay? I haven't gotten to that part yet!
Can I borrow your copy of Dr Phogg's Guide to Invis-Ability?
No way, I'm not done with it yet.
How's the book going?
It's become quite melancholy, I'm not sure what to make of it.
A lot more rhyming, I imagine?
How did you know?
Just a hunch.
Have you seen the doctor's briefcase around?
Can't say that I have, sorry!
Do you think Mr Masson will be okay?
He'll be sporting a headache and a sizable bar tab to settle, but I'm fairly confident that he'll recover.
I should really get going.
Don't be a stranger!
What were you calling yourselves again?
The Order Of Idle Hands!
Since its inception, the order has gently nudged Lady Unterwald's business endeavours.
However, I must admit, tonight's events have caught us all off guard.
What are you doing about Lady Unterwald?
Our first order of business is to get that will and testament back.
Are you making any progress with the safe you discovered?
I'm still working on it!
Just let us know when you've got that safe open, and we'll take it from there!
Nice robes, did you make them yourselves?
They were sourced from a small, independent seller.
His mother, if you must know.
She's a wonderful seamstress!
Have you seen a medical briefcase around here?
Sorry Arthur, I'm afraid we've been a little distracted.
What with the murder and everything?
Yes, the murder. Thank you for reminding me.
What's with the gentleman on the sofa?
Doctor Hirsch brought him in this afternoon, it seems he went a bit overboard with the drinks.
Not to worry, though, Maurice is keeping an eye on him for us.
Isn't that right, Maurice?
Mm hm.
Any idea when he'll be back to his senses?
Judging by his current condition, I doubt it'll be any time soon.
I'll be going now.
Speak soon.
I'm afraid not, but I'll make a mental note!
If anyone comes across it, you'll be the first to know!
Any ideas on how to get Lady Unterwald's safe open?
That depends, what kind of locks are we working with?
The safe has two mechanisms. A combination lock and a voice-activated lock.
The combination sounds simple enough. It's likely a date or number sequence.
But a voice activated lock..
How's your Lady Unterwald impression?
Far from convincing, I'm afraid.
What's on the itinerary for today?
Oh, don't even get me started.
With the death of Lady Unterwald, my entire agenda just went up in smoke!
What an inconvenience!
I know! I'm going to have to start the whole thing from scratch.
How is the new itinerary coming along?
I'm still trying to formulate a new agenda.
So far I've written down ‘Recover the last will and testament of Lady Unterwald'
How are you doing on that end?
I'm still working on that.
Any updates on the itinerary?
Still just that one item, Mr Ackerman.
Are you any closer to recovering Lady Unterwald's will?
I'm working on it!
Is this level of secrecy really necessary?
Back when I first joined, a simple nod and a wink sufficed.
Then, we transitioned to the passwords.
After that it was the handshakes.
Now Brother Jared is researching invisible ink!
You can't stop the march of progression, Gretchen!
See you around!
Where can I get a drink?
You'll have to enquire at the bar, sir.
What's this I'm hearing about a rodent problem?
Nothing to concern yourself with, sir.
Some of the passengers are complaining about missing valuables.
They believe a common rodent to be stealing from them.
So there isn't a rodent sneaking around stealing jewellery?
The Reuss Express is vermin free, I assure you.
I suspect certain passengers have merely been careless with their valuables.
Is it too late to order from the kitchen?
I'm afraid the kitchen is temporarily closed for repairs.
What repairs are taking place in the kitchen?
Ah, there's nothing to be concerned about.
I believe the kitchen staff encountered an overzealous health inspector.
Do you know when the kitchen will reopen?
I'm sure things will be up and running again shortly.
Just as soon as the kitchen staff have regained their composure.
Did you see anything during Lady Unterwald's speech?
Apart from a traumatic event I shall never recover from?
Yes, of course. Did you see anything suspicious?
We were all thrown into darkness, as you well know.
If you're asking me to identify a suspect, I can't help you.
I'll see you around!
It's Doctor Hirsch's medical bag. I assume it's full of doctorly things.
Let's try this one more time.
You know, you're starting to feel like bad luck, kid!
Step away from the table, pronto.
I ain't messing around no more.
All on red.
All on black.
Bad luck old chap.
Never mind, at least you tried!
Oh dear!
That's not possible!
Uh, excuse me.
Eegh!
Oooh!
Oww!
Arghh!
Alright, sto-
Oooh! Ahhh!
Ooh! Not the face!!
Ouch.
I guess the house always wins.
Psst.
Over here.
Right this way, sir.
Are you ready?
Ready!
Then let us begin!
Show me, exaltation!
What a big smile, beautiful!
Give me contemplation!
Ah, I can see you're thinking very hard!
For this next one, you're flabbergasted!
Oui, oui! You've never looked more confused!
Ah, pure perfection!
I feel rejuvenated, thank you, Arthur.
Don't mention it!
Pierre managed to capture the handshakes in the background of these sketches!
I should take them to Dr Hirsch and see what he can tell me.
Come back when you know what you're doing, kid.
Don't waste my time, kid.
Uh, hello?
Oh boy.
It's ol' clammy hands again.
I'm afraid the Reuss Express has been slipping in standards for some time now.
But to have vermin aboard the train, have things really got so bad?
I'm telling you, it was as big as a house cat!
How revolting!
I heard the Lady took a tumble on stage during her big speech.
Oh my, I hope she's not too badly hurt!
Hard to tell, they're keeping it all hush-hush.
I heard Lady Unterwald's bumbling attorney lost her will and testament!
Really? How awful!
It was quite a sight to behold, apparently.
He was chasing down the carriage after it!
Sleeper Carriage.
Kitchen Carriage.
Kitchen Pantry.
Service Carriages.
I imagine it's a fun way to lose all your savings.
You're half right, I'm not having much fun.
I'm not sure I know the rules.
Besides, it makes me dizzy.
I wouldn't want to be the poor sap who has to dust a moving chandelier.
''CHEATING STRICTLY PROHIBITED.''
''THERE IS TO BE NO: CARD-COUNTING, MONEY LAUNDERING, CHEATING THE SYSTEM, WINNING TOO FREQUENTLY, EXPLOITATION OF EVERYDAY ITEMS AND/OR NATURAL PHENOMENA.''
''RULE BREAKERS WILL FIND THEMSELVES IMMEDIATELY EJECTED FROM THE PREMISES.''
Ejected?
Oh yes, hun. Usually they go straight out the window.
Unterwald Carriages.
April, are you there?
Diana?
What took you so long? I was starting to worry!
I have to go. I'll keep you updated.
Diana, abort! Abort the mission!
So, you finally made it.
I was beginning to doubt your abilities!
You didn't make it easy!
Were you talking to someone in here?
No. And that's none of your concern.
Well, what can you tell me?
Hm, you're right. A proper introduction is in order.
Diana Osterhagen, Inland Revenue Secret Service.
I'm a field operative, working under the British Government.
The Inland Revenue has a Secret Service branch? I've never heard of them.
That's the point, Arthur.
We've suspected the Unterwald estate has been concealing financial crimes for some time, but we weren't able to pin them down.
There was always an obstruction, someone with their thumb on the scale.
Not just a thumb, but maybe a hand.
We had nothing to go on, not until an informant made contact with the promise of information.
And...
You think I'm that informant?
The informant would be wearing a blue suit with a red rosette.
Are you suggesting that doesn't match your description?
The suit? Of course.
Lady Unterwald must have orchestrated this whole thing!
What's that?
Nothing! I was just thinking out loud.
So, what have you got? Do you have evidence of financial misconduct?
I need to find out who killed Lady Unterwald, or I could be the next one to vanish!
I'll need to talk to the other passengers, maybe they saw something.
Lady Unterwald's quarters could hold some clues.
Thanks for dealing with Don, Arthur.
I know you didn't have to help me, considering the circumstances.
I still have a responsibility to the estate, and Don was gambling estate funds.
Quite right, quite right.
One last thing, I believe the doctor was looking to speak with you.
They were?
Indeed. I believe he's just about managed to pull himself together.
You'll find him in Lady Unterwald's quarters, no doubt combing over her personal effects.
Alright, I'll check up on him.
I'll be in the lounge if you need me.
Psst! We need to talk.
Psst, over here!
Psst, get over here!
Hey! Come this way.
There's a satisfying undulation to the water's motion.
Are these lemons free?
Do you actually want the lemons?
Hm, I might do.
They're filled with nondescript types of brown liquid.
I'm not sure who'd drink these willingly.
They're an acquired taste.
Ladder hemstitch, mitered corners, 100% white linen.
These are some high-end cocktail napkins!
You should expect nothing less on the Reuss Express.
''Please wait to be seated.''
Hm.
I guess it's more of a suggestion.
That should be all of them.
I better find somewhere to hide, and fast!
This damn watch must be on the fritz.
At this rate I'm gonna run out of chips!
Wait a second...
No, I've been robbed!
So this is what it feels like...
Okay, Don.
The jig is up.
I owe a lot of money.
No need to panic.
I can jump off at the next bend.
Yeah, maybe cross at the border.
Greetings, Mr Donato.
Might we ask to have a friendly chat.
About your most recent gambling activities?
S-Sure thing.
A most unscrupulous individual is gambling with counterfeit chips.
F-Fake chips?
We suspect this individual has also taken a creative approach to magnetism.
An unsanctioned use of physical phenomena.
M-Magnetism?
The capacity to attract and repulse forces between objects.
I wouldn't know anything about that.
Then allow my associate to demonstrate...
Hey, who switched off the lights!
Between the two of us, I'm not the bad guy, y'hear?
Ah, so it's all my fault.
I suppose in your mind I bankrupted the company? I killed Lady Unterwald?
Don't be so absurd. We're done here.
You're not done until I say so.
I have a feeling the authorities would find THIS very compelling.
...I killed Lady Unterwald.
You've been RECORDING?!
When you're in my line of work you need a little insurance, y'know? Consider it an incentive to stay in line.
Besides, I've got a new scheme in play. I'm telling ya, Bergmann. I won't lose this time!
You better be right.
It sounds like Bergmann has fallen in with the wrong crowd.
I should get my hands on that ledger in Lady Unterwald's quarters.
I'd better get out the way again.
Damn thievin' casino.
I'm supposed to be stealin' from them!
Eh, no matter.
Still got plenty of chips left.
Should be enough to get my winnings back.
And then some!
There's nothing in there I need.
That's a seriously powerful magnet.
Ugh.
A bit garish for my taste, but this is the honeymoon suite.
I guess Don's been winning big at the casino.
I'll bet these look convincing with a lick of paint.
I have no clue what these are for, but I bet Don's up to something shady.
Don must be using these fraudulent chips to cheat in the casino.
Don was gambling with fraudulent chips, what a slimeball!
There are piles of wooden casino chips in these boxes.
Seems like Don is stirring up trouble for the casino.
Bergmann said Don was scamming the casino using magnetism and fake chips.
These are all that's left of Don's gambling scheme.
If I seal up these burrows, I'd have a better chance of catching the mouse.
A tiny entrance for an unwanted guest.
They've settled into quite a hypnotic pattern.
Arthur Ackerman. We've been expecting you for some time.
You have?
Another newbie? Which one is this?
The uninitiated one.
The who?
You know, the dummy.
What's going on here?
Come forth, my child.
Take my hand, let us see what the future has in store for you.
You're going to read my palm?
One moment.
Ahh, yes, I see it now.
